Hello everyone,

My name is Yanting Teng, and I have been trying to learn more about lean for a few months. Most recently, I have been interested in formalizing Schur Weyl duality. Given this result seems standard and can be stated abastractly, I wanted to ask if it is in the scope of mathlib?

A little bit about my background: I am currenty a postdoc working n theoretical physics. My motivation comes from the application of the result in quantum information theory. I have used AI quite a lot so far downstream, but would be really keen to learn how to write mathlib standard proper definitions.

I would appreicate any thoughts you have. Thank you!
Best,
Yanting
Are you also interested in the symmetric functions side?

It would be lovely to have this in Mathlib.

(I have an AI-written formalization of Schur-Weyl duality, as part of a complete formalization of Etingof's "Representation Theory" textbook, but it requires more polish to get even to a "reusable by others" level, and might not be useful for someone trying to do a Mathlib-level formalization of this material.)

Per Alexandersson said:

Are you also interested in the symmetric functions side?

Hello I think for my personal goal of applying Schur Weyl duality to quantum info, it may not show up directly. But Im interested to hear is there something specific about it that you have in mind?

Hi thanks for the thoughts! Good to know it is of interest to the community already.
I would be very happy to spend some time to work on some basic definitions of permutation actions on tensor powers. It seems there is already a good amount of API in TensorProduct and PiTensorProduct so at least Im not totally starting from scratch.

For instance, I can open a PR and ask for feedbacks on a basic definition such as the action of a tensor product of operators. Does this sound like a reasonable first step?
I am not yet at the mathlib level myself and also have some LLM generated code, but I am very interested in learning how to write good code!

Hi Kim hi Alexandersson,

Hope you are well.

Just want to follow up on this that I have started a PR to mathlib: https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/pull/41781.
I added the most basic definitions on permutation action and the image of permutation operators.

Would very much appreciate it if you have any thoughts or suggestions. Thanks!

Best,
Yanting
